description:
Caches hold one entry fewer than their `maxsize`.

`LRUCache(maxsize=3)` evicts an entry as soon as the third key is inserted, so it never holds more than two items: `len(cache)` and `cache.currsize` top out at 2. With a custom `getsizeof`, values whose sizes add up to exactly `maxsize` do not fit together either — in a cache with `maxsize=10`, storing a value of size 4 and then one of size 6 evicts the first.

Every cache class is affected, which points at the shared eviction logic in `Cache.__setitem__`; the existing tests in `tests/test_cache.py` and `tests/test_lru.py` fail (`test_insert`, `test_lru`, `test_update`, ...). A cache must be allowed to fill up to exactly `maxsize`.
bug_patch:
diff --git a/src/cachetools/__init__.py b/src/cachetools/__init__.py
index e992f5c..86f5f67 100644
--- a/src/cachetools/__init__.py
+++ b/src/cachetools/__init__.py
@@ -83,7 +83,7 @@ class Cache(collections.abc.MutableMapping):
             raise ValueError("value too large")
         if key not in self.__data:
             diffsize = size
-            while self.__currsize + diffsize > maxsize:
+            while self.__currsize + diffsize >= maxsize:
                 self.popitem()
         else:
             diffsize = size - self.__size[key]

hidden_test_patch:
diff --git a/tests/test_repopilot_cachetools_004.py b/tests/test_repopilot_cachetools_004.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..d17d1e7
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_repopilot_cachetools_004.py
@@ -0,0 +1,18 @@
+from cachetools import Cache, LRUCache
+
+
+def test_cache_can_be_filled_up_to_maxsize():
+    cache = LRUCache(maxsize=3)
+    for key in "abc":
+        cache[key] = key
+    assert len(cache) == 3
+    assert cache.currsize == 3
+    assert set(cache) == {"a", "b", "c"}
+
+
+def test_values_whose_sizes_sum_exactly_to_maxsize_fit():
+    cache = Cache(maxsize=10, getsizeof=lambda value: value)
+    cache["a"] = 4
+    cache["b"] = 6
+    assert len(cache) == 2
+    assert cache.currsize == 10
